clue.text: Purge using concoction of bitter aloe

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture brewed up, so the letters of the two words that follow are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A herbal remedy: a bitter aloe brew taken as a purgative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Purge' looks like a medical purge to go with the aloe, but here it means wipe out completely.
explanation.definitionFit: To purge something is to eliminate it entirely, a synonym for wiping it out.

clue.text: Lifted ladle dropping end? Silly me!

indicators.note: in a down clue lifted means turned upwards, so the word is read from bottom to top
dropping end means the last letter of the word is lost

parts.note: a ladle is a kind of large spoon

explanation.surface: A cook drops the ladle and apologises for the clumsiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping end' turns SPOON into SPOO, and 'Lifted' reads that upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation said after making a small mistake, an interjection of apology.

clue.text: Left in saddle breaking runaway

indicators.note: breaking means smashed up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rider left in the saddle while breaking a bolting horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runaway' suggests a bolting horse, but it is the runaway victory.
explanation.definitionFit: A runaway win at an election is an overwhelming victory, the sense here.

clue.text: Coach possibly coaches

definitions.meaning: to coach someone is to teach or drill them
a set of railway carriages, which may be called coaches, joined together

explanation.surface: A sports coach, wondering whether he will be coaching.
explanation.definitionFit: To coach is to instruct, and a railway set is made of linked coaches.

clue.text: Lie concerned with Conservative policy

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a party line is its policy

explanation.surface: An accusation that a Tory policy is founded on a falsehood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lie' looks like a falsehood but means lie back.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie back at rest is to lean or recline, the verb meaning to rest horizontally.

clue.text: Later today drunk takes refusal the wrong way

indicators.note: takes means holds inside, so the word for drunk takes the other piece within it

parts.note: tight is slang for drunk

indicators.note: the wrong way says the word for refusal is turned around

parts.note: no is a refusal

explanation.surface: A drunk taking a rejection badly later in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way' turns the refusal around, and 'takes' puts the result inside the slang word for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: This evening is the part of the present day still to come, a synonym.

clue.text: United following team's card

indicators.note: the letter for United comes after the word for team, so following sets the order

parts.note: a team's players are its men
U is the standard abbreviation for United, as in football club names

explanation.surface: A football fan studying Manchester United's teamsheet or programme.
explanation.definitionFit: In a restaurant the card listing the dishes is the bill of fare, a synonym.

clue.text: Tiredness for all in unlimited sport

indicators.note: in puts the rating letter inside the trimmed sport
unlimited removes the limits, the first and last letters of the word

parts.note: tennis is a sport
U is the British film rating for a universal audience, suitable for all

explanation.surface: Fatigue for everyone after a sport played without limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unlimited' trims TENNIS to ENNI, and 'in' places U inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A listless weariness from boredom is a kind of tiredness, a near synonym.

clue.text: Free, not having been booked

definitions.meaning: open and frank, without holding back
a seat not reserved in advance

explanation.surface: A free seat, one nobody had booked.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrestrained in manner is one sense; seats not booked ahead are the other.

clue.text: Animal also carried by father

indicators.note: being carried by something means sitting inside it, so the word for also goes inside the word for father

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: A dad carrying a child's toy animal, or a zoo trip.
explanation.definitionFit: The black-and-white bear of China is an example of an animal.

clue.text: Can or tin formed to hold preserve finally?

definitions.text: Can or tin formed to hold preserve finally?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the extra letter inside them
the letters of the three words are formed into a new shape, an anagram signal
finally picks the last letter of the word preserve

explanation.surface: A cannery question: can or tin, shaped to hold preserved food.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: 'formed' rearranges the letters of 'Can or tin', and 'to hold' puts the final letter of 'preserve' inside them, which together describe a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A can or tin made to keep preserved food is a typical receptacle, as the question mark admits.

clue.text: Sceptic hates it to be otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise means in another way, so the letters of the two words are arranged differently

explanation.surface: A doubter who loathes the idea of anything being different.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-believer in God is a religious sceptic.

clue.text: Polishing some bars and ingots

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A metalworker buffing up a stock of metal bars and ingots.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbing a surface smooth with abrasive paper is a form of polishing it.

clue.text: Expressed arrogance of those due to succeed

indicators.note: expressed means spoken out, so the word that follows is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: putting on airs is a show of arrogance

explanation.surface: A sneer at the haughty manner of an aristocrat's offspring.
explanation.walkthrough: AIRS and HEIRS sound alike because the H of the second is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Successors to a title or estate are the people next in line to inherit it.

clue.text: Craftsman worked hard accepting need's minute

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the word for worked holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: a brake or a measure that bit took effect, that worked
need's, read as need is, gives lacks
H is the standard abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: An artisan who toiled, meeting a need within a minute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked' means took effect, as when a new rule bit; 'need's' must be read as 'need is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A forge worker shaping iron is a traditional craftsman.

clue.text: Regularly sleep in, having guaranteed free time

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the words that follow, the second, fourth and sixth

parts.note: something guaranteed is sure, certain

explanation.surface: Someone enjoying a lie-in, sure of a day off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes the even letters of SLEEPIN: L, E, I.
explanation.definitionFit: Hours spent at ease, away from work, are a synonym for spare hours.

clue.text: Rude man flashing, exposed

indicators.note: flashing suggests moving rapidly in all directions, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crude man flashing in public, exposing himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exposed' fits the flasher, but here means unprotected, without weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Without weapons means defenceless, so left exposed to attack.

clue.text: Time ship worker set off

parts.note: a rigger fits and works the ropes and rigging of a ship

explanation.surface: A clock in for a dockyard worker on the night shift.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off an alarm or a reaction is to start it, a synonym.

clue.text: Talk purchasing posh drinks raised in bar

indicators.note: purchasing means taking hold of, so the word for talk holds the rest

parts.note: gab is idle talk

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means read upwards, so the pieces are turned around

parts.note: U is the label for upper-class usage, so posh
ports are fortified wines, drinks

explanation.surface: Chatter over buying fancy drinks lifted at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns the posh letter and the drinks upside down in this down clue; 'purchasing' puts them inside the word for talk. 'Drinks' are fortified wines from Portugal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub serving restaurant food is a kind of bar.

clue.text: Place hollow elm in box and burn

indicators.note: place says one piece is set down inside another
in says the emptied tree goes inside the box

parts.note: a crate is a wooden box

indicators.note: hollow empties a word, keeping only its outer letters

explanation.surface: Funeral instructions: an elm coffin, placed in its box, then burnt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hollow' empties the tree's name to its outer letters, and 'Place ... in' sets them inside the box.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispose of a body by burning it to ashes is the specific sense here.

clue.text: Sweetheart with partner harbouring a new issue

parts.note: the heart of the word sweet is its central letter E

indicators.note: harbouring means sheltering inside, so the word for partner holds the next pieces

parts.note: a mate is a partner

explanation.surface: A sweetheart and partner sheltering a new problem in the relationship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' looks like a noun, but is the verb to flow out.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue from a source is to come or flow from it, a synonym.

clue.text: Part is tempting embracing actress, say

indicators.note: the words before embracing hold the answer within them, running across the word breaks

explanation.surface: A role so juicy that it lures a leading actress.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer such as an actress or singer is a professional entertainer; 'say' marks the example.

clue.text: Article arrived comprising of French scholarly world

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: comprising means containing, so the word for arrived holds the French word inside it

parts.note: came means arrived
de is French for of

explanation.surface: A report that a French article has reached academic circles.
explanation.definitionFit: Universities and their scholars form the academic community, the scholarly world.

clue.text: Scene of depravity overlooking morals initially

definitions.text: Scene of depravity overlooking morals initially

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the five preceding words

explanation.surface: A town where depravity reigned, with morals ignored from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: the biblical city destroyed for wickedness disregarded morals.
explanation.definitionFit: The Biblical city burned for its wickedness is a byword for a den of vice.

clue.text: Scraps of potato served up around meal's starter

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the turned word goes around the other letter
in a down clue served up means read upwards

parts.note: spud is slang for a potato

indicators.note: starter means the first letter of the word meal

explanation.surface: Leftover bits of potato served round a meal's first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns SPUD to DUPS, with M from 'meal's starter' inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Scraps as a verb means throws away, discards, the same as getting rid of.

clue.text: Fitter going after plug for electrical device

indicators.note: the word for fitter comes after the word for plug

parts.note: a plug is a piece of promotion, an advertisement or ad
fitter means more apt

explanation.surface: An electrician wiring a plug before fitting a device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fitter' and 'plug' pretend to be electrical, but are a comparative adjective and a publicity mention.
explanation.definitionFit: A connector that lets a plug fit a different socket is an electrical gadget, here called a device.

clue.text: Lifting one newspaper's short title

definitions.meaning: the short name of the Financial Times is two words, a definite article and initials

explanation.surface: Lifting the masthead of a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: Split into two words, the answer reads as the abbreviated title of the Financial Times, a London business daily.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifting is slang for stealing; the second sense is a newspaper's shortened name.

clue.text: Occasionally play Greek instrument

indicators.note: occasionally picks letters now and then, every second one of the two words

explanation.surface: A musician who sometimes plays a Greek instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A small harp of ancient Greece is a stringed instrument.

clue.text: Wasted time, aimed to be prompt

indicators.note: wasted means ruined or wrecked, so the letters of the next two words are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A procrastinator who squandered time while meaning to be punctual.
explanation.definitionFit: A prompt reply is one given at once, with no delay, a synonym.

clue.text: Vacuous English politician facing vacuous Tory

indicators.note: facing places the politician before the next piece

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: vacuous means emptied, so only the outside letters of the word remain

explanation.surface: A political jibe: an airheaded English MP opposite a vapid Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Vacuous means lacking ideas or content, the same as hollow and devoid of substance.

clue.text: Wash old socks

definitions.meaning: to wash a car or yard down with a jet of water from a flexible pipe
an old word for stockings and socks, legwear

explanation.surface: Washing a pair of tired old socks.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden pipe is used to wash things down, and the word is an archaic term for legwear.

clue.text: Attractive Democrat fit for office?

parts.note: someone fit for office could win at the polls

explanation.surface: A glamorous Democratic candidate who looks the part for high office.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'fit for office' is being used loosely as 'able to be voted in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Delightful and appealing, a synonym for attractive or tempting.
